Voat as it currently stands is beset by a number of potential deaths. Granting administrators too much authority will result in zealous individuals skewing debates in their favor and limiting free speech. However if they adopt a hands off approach then moderators are free to usurp their power, working behind the scenes to create moderator monopolies. Lastly there's the people. Democratic ideals are excellent for ensuring that moderators serve the users over their own interests, however if left unchecked could result in subverse imperialism.

These various powers need to be separated and various checks and balances need to be put in place to ensure neither group can come to dominate the rest. I propose the creation of a council elected by the general population of Voat. Since this is a cross section of the general population no individual subverse will be able to brigade and subvert the democratic processes of smaller subverses. This council will be charged with responsibilities depending on the size of the subverse. On smaller subverses they will be in charge of moderating the "meta-discussion" of the subverse (i'll explain that later). Larger subverses are more prone to manipulation therefore they will be granted the power to accept or reject motions to add or remove moderators that are proposed by the users of that subverse.

Transparency is not required of a council member however it is heavily encouraged through democratic process. As people are more likely to vote for users that they trust anonymity will become a liability. This should help avoid the behind-the-scenes style administration that plagues reddit, which inevitably results in backroom deals and the exchanging of moderator privileges. An elected council avoids this problem since council members gain power not by appeasing other council members or moderators, but instead by appealing to users. Moderators are also unable to exchange favors and must also appease the council and their userbase.

All these structures would be effective on their own if the system itself wasn't vulnerable to the same kind of underhanded censorship that makes it impossible for reddit to respond to corruption. To prevent subverses from devolving into soft totalitarian the creation of a separate channel of communication between users should be created. The "meta-discussion" tab will be made available on every subverse. It will function much like a regular subverse while being restricted to text posts only. It will serve as a place to discuss the state of the subverse and to vote on proposals regarding the moderation. Unlike a regular subverse it will be moderated by the council and its delegates. Providing multiple channels for users to stay informed will ensure incriminating information will never be held from the users who can then use their democratic powers to fight corruption in the system.

That's enough of my ramblings for tonight as you can tell this is only a rough draft and I'm sure there's about a million different contingencies I haven't accounted for. Let me know if there's something you think I missed or you wish to make an amendment.
